previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a two-week history of nonproductive cough and shortness of breath. A chest X-ray revealed left lower lobe pneumonia, and she was started on IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin, with oxygen support initially at 2 liters per minute. Her oxygen needs improved within 1.5 days, and she was weaned to room air. She remained stable throughout the admission, with normal blood pressure and kidney function. Her home medications for hypertension, diastolic heart failure, and hyperlipidemia were continued. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics, including cefpodoxime and azithromycin, with adjustments to her furosemide dosing and instructions to follow a 2-gram sodium diet and monitor daily weight. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider.

creatinine.

hospitalization to a creatinine of 1.3 from baseline of 0.7-0.8. 
 This was likely secondary to contrast induced nephropathy 
versus pre-renal azotemia.  Patient received IVF hydration, and 
her creatinine on the day of discharge had returned to baseline 
at 0.7.

hospital course. She was initially continued on home furosemide, 
which was held when patient developed acute renal failure.

radiology_notes.text:
SINGLE VIEW OF THE CHEST:  

HISTORY:  ___ woman with cough, fever, shortness of breath and
hypoxia.  Assess for infiltrate.

COMPARISON:  A series of chest x-rays, most recently ___ dating back to
___.

FINDINGS:  A single portable semi-upright AP view of the chest was obtained.
Lung volumes are low.  Cardiomegaly and tortuosity of the aorta are stable. No
airspace consolidation or large effusion is identified, although the
retrocardiac area is difficult to assess on this frontal view.

Bilateral nodular pleural thickening is stable.  There are stable degenerative
changes of the shoulder.

IMPRESSION:  Limited single view study without acute intrathoracic process.
Please refer to CT chest performed concurrently.

TWO-VIEW STUDY OF THE CHEST

HISTORY:  ___ woman with shortness of breath, difficult portable chest
x-ray to evaluate.  Please evaluate for infiltrate.

COMPARISON:  Portable chest x-ray from today (___) at 8:54 a.m., a series
of chest x-rays from ___ through ___ and CTA of the chest,
___.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  Lung volumes
are low.  There is no focal airspace consolidation.  The retrocardiac space is
clear. The cardiac silhouette is top normal in size. Areas of peripheral
pleural nodularity are unchanged. There is scoliosis of the thoracic spine and
degenerative change of the shoulders. 

IMPRESSION:  Low lung volumes.  No evidence of pneumonia. Please refer to CT
chest performed subsequently.

CTA OF THE CHEST WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST

HISTORY:  ___ female with initial hypoxia on arrival, no infiltrate on
chest x-ray.  Please evaluate for pulmonary embolism.

COMPARISON:  CTA of the chest ___ and ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CTA images of the chest were obtained following
administration of intravenous contrast.  Prior to administration of contrast,
MDCT images of the chest were obtained.  Multiplanar reformatted images were
generated.

FINDINGS:  NON-CONTRAST CT OF THE CHEST:  There is no intramural hematoma.

CTA OF THE CHEST:  There are bilateral pulmonary emboli.  There are right
lobar, segmental and subsegmental pulmonary emboli of the right upper and
right lower lobes. Segmental and subsegmental pulmonary emboli also noted in
the left lower lobe.  These are best appreciated on images 3:34 and 3:52.
There is no evidence of right heart strain.

A right upper lobe nodule (3:40) measures 9 x 6 mm, and is stable in
comparison to CTA chest ___.  Prevascular and hilar lymph nodes are
not pathologically enlarged by size criteria.  Foci of prominent extrapleural
fat are stable. Evaluation of the lung bases is limited by motion. Scattered
ground glass opacities in the lungs likely reflect expiratory phase and
hypoventilatory effects. 

The thoracic aorta is normal in caliber. Atheroma is noted in the aorta at the
level of the diaphragm.

There is a low-density lesion within the left lobe of the thyroid, not
completely imaged on this study but appears stable in comparison to ___.

Limited imaging through the upper abdomen demonstrates a small hiatal hernia.
There are mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.  No suspicious
lytic or blastic osseous lesion is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral pulmonary emboli involving branches of the right upper and right
lower lobes, and left lower lobe. No evidence of right heart strain. Findings
were posted to the Emergency Department dashboard following initial review.
